title: ISEYC national evidence snapshots
note: Dated transcriptions from the linked publisher sources. These are not a continuously refreshed data feed. Every value retains its own reference period, geography, evidence type and limitations.

records.title: WHO · Nigeria health indicators
records.evidenceType: WHO country profile · indicator-specific estimates and reported series
limitations: WHO indicator reference years differ; do not present these values as one current-year snapshot or as Kaduna State figures.
Under-five mortality, neonatal mortality and maternal mortality are statistical estimates and retain their uncertainty intervals.
The WHO profile currently shows no 2023 value for new HIV infections; no substitute value is used.
WHO reports Nigerian death-registration data as unavailable or unusable for cause-of-death analysis; cause-of-death estimates require caution.
Workforce, immunisation, WASH and expenditure indicators have different source methods and must not be combined as if they share one measurement process.
National values do not establish state, LGA, facility or household outcomes.
records.interpretation: Use as national health context and as a map of questions for deeper investigation. Preserve each indicator's reference year and measurement type. Do not use these national estimates to grade an individual facility or state programme.

records.title: NIMC · National identity enrolment
limitations: Enrolment records are not a population census, active identity count or measure of access to services.
Do not calculate coverage without a compatible population denominator, reference year and methodology.
This is a historical dashboard snapshot, not a live 2026 figure.
Kaduna State is not Kaduna South; no LGA-level value is inferred.
records.interpretation: Useful for understanding identity-registration administration and geographic distribution, not as a direct measure of citizenship, service access or population coverage.

records.title: NITDA · Digital Literacy for All

geography.label: Nigeria · 36 states + FCT, LGAs and communities

records.evidenceType: Government programme dashboard · verified training records
limitations: The dashboard's verified-beneficiary definition and deduplication method must be obtained before comparison with other programmes.
Training or completion records do not independently establish durable competence, employment outcomes or population-wide digital literacy.
The 70% by 2027 and 95% by 2030 targets are targets, not achieved outcomes.
The 5.57% figure is progress against the programme's 50 million target, not Nigeria's national digital literacy rate.
Programme dashboard data are source-reported and should not be described as independently audited by ISEYC.
records.interpretation: A strong operational source for tracking the digital-skills programme and its geographic reach. It can inform ISEYC's Software & Technology and Education departments, but must not be confused with a national digital-literacy prevalence survey. The dashboard also reports inclusion and partner participation; contributor totals may overlap and should not be summed as unique people.

records.title: NASENI · InnovateNaija challenge
records.publisher: National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure · NASENI Innovation Hub
records.referencePeriod: Announcement · 3 September 2025; current campaign page reviewed 9 November 2026
limitations: These are announced programme terms, not evidence that the funds were disbursed.
The announcement's planned selection and final event dates do not prove that winners were selected or products commercialised.
No independently verified beneficiary, grant-disbursement, product-readiness or employment outcome dataset is integrated here.
The official campaign page states that applications are closed and Phase 2 voting has ended; this does not identify verified winners or prove that any announced grant was paid.
records.interpretation: Treat as an innovation-policy and programme activity record. Upgrade its status only when official selection, award, disbursement and outcome evidence is obtained.

records.title: NBS · Real GDP growth
limitations: This is a national quarterly GDP estimate, not a measure of household welfare or local economic conditions.
The NBS GDP series was rebased; preserve the base year and methodology when comparing across vintages.
This is not a Kaduna State or LGA growth rate.
The linked catalogue lists the Q1 2026 report; the exact table and rebasing notes should be retained with any production indicator record.
records.interpretation: Use as national economic context only. The Observatory should extract and validate the original NBS table before treating this snapshot as a reusable time series.

records.title: ISN · Nigerian Innovation Hub Assessment
records.referencePeriod: Summary released 22 May 2026 · survey reference period not stated in summary

geography.label: Nigeria · six geopolitical zones and named state/city clusters

records.evidenceType: Industry ecosystem assessment summary · survey findings as reported by ISN

metrics.label: Active and partially active ecosystem spaces
Hubs with fewer than 10 full-time employees

additionalMetrics.label: Kano, Kaduna, Enugu, Rivers and Abia
Hubs with annual revenue below US$50,000
Four leading focus areas combined
additionalMetrics.measurementType: survey respondent share · ICT/Software, AgriTech, FinTech, EdTech

limitations: The public article is an executive summary; sample frame, collection period, respondent definitions, weighting and full methodology require the full report.
Geographic percentages are described as shares of respondents, not a census share of all Nigerian hubs or absolute hub counts.
More than 190 active hubs surveyed/covered and an ecosystem of more than 250 active and partially active spaces are different denominators; do not combine them.
Percentages for staffing, training, mentorship, revenue and power outages are survey-summary findings and should be attributed to ISN.
The 2026–2030 funding and startup support figures are strategic targets, not achieved results.
The directory and assessment summary do not establish current operational capacity or local outcomes for any individual hub.
records.interpretation: Use this assessment to understand structural constraints in Nigeria's innovation ecosystem and design capacity-building, digital-skills and partnership programmes. Treat it as a survey summary, not a complete national census or a live performance dashboard.
